summary: Ukraine's Prosecutor General publishes the citizenship of every identified suspect by offence, including offences against children, but child victims by citizenship only as one all-offence total. Citizenship is a proxy, ethnicity is not recorded, and the data exclude occupied territories.

nations.National (Office of the Prosecutor Gener: Unified reports on criminal offences (Form 1) and on persons who committed them (Form 2).

european_title: Not recorded by any Ukrainian source
european_note: Ukrainian crime statistics record only citizenship (Ukrainian, foreign or stateless), never ethnicity. Almost everyone involved is a Ukrainian citizen, a group that includes many ethnic groups, so ethnic Europeans cannot be identified.
proxy_note: Ukraine records citizenship only, never ethnicity. Every group below is a proxy, not ethnicity.

harms.label: Sexual offences and offences against children
harms.intro: Form 2 identified 3,008 people for criminal offences against children in 2025: 2,996 Ukrainian and 12 foreign citizens. For sexual offences (all victims) it identified 327 people (322 Ukrainian, 3 foreign, 2 stateless) and for corruption of minors (Art. 156) 54, all Ukrainian. Form 1 counts 348 child victims of rape, 193 of sexual violence, 158 of sexual acts with a child under 16 and 173 of corruption of minors, with no citizenship. Form 1 (section 7) counts 7,437 child victims of all criminal offences in 2025 (3,860 aged 14-17 and 3,577 under 14). Among victims who were foreigners, illegal migrants, refugees or stateless persons (1,167 of all ages), 10 were children (4 aged 14-17, 6 under 14), so about 0.1% of child victims were not Ukrainian citizens. This total covers every offence, including war crimes and road deaths, and is not split by harm.

breakdown.why: The Prosecutor General's Form 2 report (2025) gives persons identified for each offence by citizenship (Ukrainian, foreign, stateless): sexual offences 327 (3 foreign, 2 stateless), corruption of minors 54 (none foreign), all offences against children 3,008 (12 foreign). Form 1 gives only an all-offence count of foreign child victims (10 of 7,437). Heritage points are 0 under the paired-data rule: no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases.

Form 2 gives persons identified for domestic violence (1,448; 7 foreign) and for all offences against children (3,008; 12 foreign). Victims by citizenship only as an all-offence total. Heritage points are 0 under the paired-data rule: no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases.

Form 2 gives persons identified for murder of a young child or a pregnant woman (Art. 115(2)(2): 15, all Ukrainian citizens) and all intentional murder (669; 7 foreign, 1 stateless). Child victims by citizenship only as the all-offence total. Heritage points are 0 under the paired-data rule: no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases.

Form 2 gives 47 persons identified for trafficking (5 foreign), all victim ages; Form 1 gives 113 trafficking victims (16 children) with no citizenship split. Heritage points are 0 under the paired-data rule: no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases.

Form 2 gives pornography offences (Art. 301: 119 persons, 2 foreign, 1 stateless) without separating child abuse material; no victims by citizenship. Heritage points are 0 under the paired-data rule: no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases.

components.name: Victim heritage
components.full: Official data by harm that separately identify ethnic European children (e.g. White non-Hispanic, White British) alongside every other group, self-reported or official, few unknowns. Broad categories that lump ethnic Europeans with others get partial credit; proxies (nationality, citizenship, migration background, country of birth) at most 9.4 points.

components.name: Perpetrator heritage
components.full: Same standard for perpetrators: not perceived, few unknowns, ethnic Europeans separately identified. Proxies at most 9.4 points.

components.name: Coverage and missing data
components.full: Over 90% of the population covered, under 10% unknown

components.name: Rates and linkage
components.full: Rates per 100,000 possible, and victim heritage linked to perpetrator heritage

score.gold_standard: 100% means a country publishes data that separately identifies ethnic Europeans, both as perpetrators (so one can tell when they disproportionately harm a group) and as child victims (so one can tell when ethnic European children are disproportionately harmed), alongside every other group, linked victim to perpetrator, for every harm. Heritage points require that link as a published cross-table for the same child cases. One-sided data scores 0 for heritage.
score.rules: Heritage is 75 of every 100 points and is awarded only for a published cross-table that records child victim heritage and offender heritage for the same cases. One-sided data scores 0 for heritage. Coverage is 10, rates 7.5 and access 7.5. Proxies such as nationality or migration background earn at most a quarter of the heritage points, and only when that pair is published. A published “White” category that merges Hispanic people or another group, so ethnic Europeans cannot be isolated, is scored as a proxy under the same cap. A country with no real ethnicity data is capped at 25%. Neglect is not part of the score.
score.why: Ukraine scores 9% on the stricter scale (0-20%). Heritage points are 0 because there is no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases. One-sided data earns no heritage credit. The Prosecutor General's monthly reports give every identified suspect's citizenship (Ukrainian, foreign or stateless) by offence, including a row for all offences against children and for the murder of a young child or pregnant woman, but child victims by citizenship only as one all-offence total. Figures exclude occupied territories and are collected under martial law.
score.weights_id: harm weights of 24 Nov 2026 (homicide 27.78, sexual abuse 22.22, sex trafficking 22.22, physical abuse 16.67, online exploitation 11.11); paired-data rule: heritage points only for a published child victim×offender cross-table

paired_child.basis: No published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases. One-sided data scores 0 for heritage.

availability_note: Each harm has an 'availability' map listing the victim and perpetrator groups with any published figure (overall and by measure) and any linked victim-perpetrator pairs. Groups not listed have no data for that harm; the explorer should grey them out rather than offer an empty combination.
